Subject: US-WEST: Prefetch/KV backlog causing degraded generation — status page update

Hi Sasha / EdgeWave team,

We wanted to notify you that between 07:05 and 08:45 UTC today we observed an elevated rate of degraded generations and higher p95 latency for hosted inference in the us-west region affecting a subset of long-context requests. We have opened incident RED-2027-11-30-03 on our status page (link below).

What happened (initial):
- Symptoms: increased p95 for generation endpoints (+3-4x typical), some responses were truncated/partial.
- Region: us-west (primary).
- Impact window: approximately 07:05–08:45 UTC, intermittent tail through 09:10 UTC for a small fraction of requests.

Immediate mitigations we applied:
1) Activated fallback routing to alternate model variant with conservative prefetch settings.
2) Scaled up our dedicated pool in us-west and drained the most impacted hosts.
3) Cleared a backlog of prefetch tasks that had accumulated behind long-sequence KV loads.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (high-level timeline) and diagnostic_logs_excerpt.txt (truncated logs showing prefetch queue growth).

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RED-2027-11-30-03
Shared drive for logs: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1A2B3C-prefetch-logs

Short term ask: if you observed any customer-visible failures or have logs (request IDs) for affected calls, please reply with them and we will correlate immediately.

We will follow up with a clearer cause analysis and remediation plan within the next 48 hours and will include the timeline and next steps. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production applications and are prioritizing a thorough postmortem and compensatory review where appropriate.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Senior SRE, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

- Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a burst of concurrent long-context inference requests caused prefetch workers to build up large KV preloads; prefetch queue growth led to backpressure and KV cache starvation on a subset of hosts, degrading generation quality.
- Immediate technical actions (already executed): clear prefetch backlog, scale pool, activate routing fallback.
- Action items for RCA (owners):
  * Full timeline correlation and request-id mapping (Marissa) — due EOD 2027-12-01.
  * Prefetch/backpressure metrics review and alert tuning (Karthik) — proposal by 2027-12-03.
  * Mitigation: implement adaptive prefetch caps for long-context requests and instrument per-tenant prefetch queue depth (Camila) — plan by 2027-12-07.

We should schedule a 30-minute postmortem call with EdgeWave and their technical contacts once we have the timeline and reproduced the signal. Suggest Wednesday 2027-12-01 16:00 UTC; I will send a calendar invite once confirmed.

Cc Logan and Marissa on externally-facing messaging. I will draft the internal RCA and then trim for the customer-facing postmortem.

Subject: Follow-up: brief RCA and next steps (incident RED-2027-11-30-03)

Hi Sasha — quick follow-up with what we have so far and immediate next steps.

Preliminary cause (short):
- Root cause: transient prefetch backlog leading to KV cache starvation on a small subset of us-west hosts. The backlog was triggered by a correlated burst of long-context generation requests from several tenants around 07:03–07:10 UTC. Prefetch workers were blocked by synchronous KV load patterns, which allowed queues to grow and increased tail latency.

Impact scope:
- Primary: generation endpoints in us-west for long-context (>8k tokens) requests.
- Embeddings: no service degradation observed for embedding endpoints — we validated embedding request rates and latency; they remained within expected bounds.

SLA assessment:
- We're still calculating exact uptime impact and will correlate request IDs you provided. At this stage it looks like partial degradation (increased error/partial responses) rather than a full-region outage. We will confirm whether this meets the contractual threshold for credits in our postmortem.

Planned customer deliverables:
1) Timeline and annotated logs (attached: incident_timeline.csv, diagnostic_logs_excerpt.txt).
2) Full RCA and remediation plan within 48 hours (deliverable by 2027-12-02).
3) Postmortem call proposal: 2027-12-01 16:00 UTC — I will follow up to confirm availability.

Technical mitigations in flight:
- Implementing per-request adaptive prefetch caps to prevent single long requests from monopolizing the prefetch queue.
- Alert tuning: add a prefetch-queue-depth alert and a KV cache eviction guard so we can auto-throttle before customer-visible impact.

Thank you again for the IDs — we will ingest and correlate them now and get back with concrete affected-request counts. If you need an immediate technical deep-dive before the postmortem, we can hop on a call.

Best,
— Logan Wright
Senior SRE, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
